question: On September 1948 the Indian army intervened and took control of which princely state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hyderabad.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Indian army intervened and took control of the princely state of Hyderabad in September 1948.**

 
 
• Hyderabad was the largest and the most prosperous princely state in India, ruled by the Nizam of Hyderabad.
 
• The Nizam initially refused to accede to either India or Pakistan after India gained independence in 1947, leading to a stand-off with the Indian government.
 
• The Indian army's intervention, code-named Operation Polo, brought an end to the stand-off and resulted in Hyderabad's accession to India.
 
 
 
• ** Assam, Uttar Pradesh, and Tripura **were not princely states but rather regular provinces of India at the time of independence in 1947.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• At the time of independence, India comprised two categories of political units,
 
 
• The British provinces (under the direct rule of the British government).
 
• The princely states (under the rule of native princes but subject to the paramountcy of the British Crown). 
 
 
 
• Of the 552 princely states situated within the geographical boundaries of India, 549 joined India and the remaining 3 (Hyderabad, Junagarh, and Kashmir) refused to join India.
 
• However, in course of time, they were also integrated with India–Hyderabad by means of police action, Junagarh by means of referendum, and Kashmir by the Instrument of Accession.
